newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger on back of U.S.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger on back of U.S.

text.p: Canadian bonds finished a shortened session higher on Friday, helped by U.S. debt markets which climbed after the release of unexpectedly weak U.S. November durable goods orders.
"They're just drifting higher on the back of the strong U.S. market," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed income analyst at Toronto-Dominion Securities Inc.
"There is no domestic influence other than just a good underlying sentiment," he added.
The Canadian benchmark 8.00 percent due 2023 added C$0.53 to C$112.05 to yield 6.993.
"Volumes have been very, very light -- almost no activity at all," Bendiksrud said.

The U.S. Commerce Department reported that durable goods fell 1.6 percent in November, compared to a revised 0.5 percent increase in October, due to weaker demand for computer components and communications equipment. The U.S. 30-year T-bond added 19/32 to 99-15/32 to yield 6.54 percent.

The Canadian dollar weakened to C$1.3701 (US$0.7298) from opening levels of C$1.3643 (US$0.7329). Traders said the unit slipped out of its expected range on unexpected selling interest from Canadian corporate investors.
The Toronto Bond Traders' Association recommended an early close for bond trading of 1200 EST/1500 GMT.
In other prices, the Canada government 7.00 percent due 2006 climbed C$0.40 to C$104.95 to yield 6.319 percent while the 6.25 of 1998 appreciated C$0.14 to C$103.74 to yield 3.955 percent.
